NEW DELHI: Congress leader Jairam Ramesh on Saturday criticised Prime Minister Narendra Modi over his remarks about "forgiving" the country's youth.He said the Prime Minister should instead apologise over a range of issues, including alleged exam paper leaks, the treatment of student protesters, demonetisation and the functioning of the Ram Mandir Trust.In a post on X, Ramesh said, "The self-declared non-biological PM enjoys playing the victim card." He further alleged that the Prime Minister "uses vile vitriol against his predecessors and political opponents" and "very frequently peddles lies to defame them, not just in his public speeches but in Parliament itself.""He uses vile vitriol against his predecessors and political opponents. He very frequently peddles lies to defame them, not just in his public speeches but in Parliament itself. He unleashes an army of foul-mouthed abusers both in Parliament and outside and gives them full protection," Ramesh said.Referring to the National Testing Agency (NTA) and student protests, Ramesh said, "the entire nation is wanting the PM to apologise for the trauma inflicted on lakhs of youth through his paper leak-ridden NTA and his Home Ministry-sanctioned brutality on student protestors."He also said the Prime Minister owed an apology over the "Chanda Chori Astha Dhoka by the Ram Mandir Trust" and for the "Tughlakian notebandi of Nov 8 2016 that destroyed crores of livelihoods and shuttered lakhs if MSMEs."Ramesh added, "but late last night, in act of supreme self-obsession, the PM said that he forgave our youth." He alleged that the remark was "an insult to the nation and to our youth", adding that young people had suffered under the government's policies and were instead seeking an apology from the Prime Minister."The Prime Minister’s InstaGram Sabhas are fooling no one," Ramesh added.Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday shared a video late at night that carried a message against abusive language and hate, saying "abuses never solve anything," amid a controversy over alleged derogatory remarks made against him by a woman from Noida during a protest in Delhi."Abuses never solve anything. Let’s guide the misguided. Let’s work together. Let’s work for Bharat," PM Modi wrote, sharing the video on X.In the video, PM Modi also highlighted the government's efforts to strengthen the country's examination system, citing Parliament's passage of a stringent anti-paper leak law."Friends, we are continuously taking one step after another to build a trustworthy examination system. Whether it is creating fast-track mechanisms or incorporating suggestions from the states, we are working in that direction."The Prime Minister said paper leaks had affected governments across the country for decades and jeopardised the future of students.PM Modi reiterated that the government would act firmly against those involved in paper leak rackets.
Article Summary: Congress leader Jairam Ramesh criticised Prime Minister Narendra Modi over his remarks about "forgiving" the country's youth. He said the PM should instead apologise over a range of issues, including alleged exam paper leaks, the treatment of student protesters, demonetisation and the functioning of the Ram Mandir Trust.

Article Title: First J&K terror attack on migrants in 21 months: Two Chhattisgarh labourers die after being shot
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The death toll in Friday night's terror attack on migrant labourers in Jammu and Kashmir's Kulgam rose to two on Saturday after a Chhattisgarh worker succumbed to injuries in hospital, officials told news agency PTI.The attack took place late Friday night in the Kelam area of south Kashmir, where the two workers were employed at a brick kiln. Officials said both men sustained critical injuries after terrorists fired at them.One of the labourers, identified as Deepak Ratray, died before he could be shifted to a hospital. The second victim, Bopinder, was initially admitted to Government Medical College (GMC) Anantnag before being referred to SKIMS Hospital in Soura, where he later succumbed to his injuries.Officials said both victims were in their twenties and had travelled from Chhattisgarh in search of work.The incident comes days after terrorists shot dead Jammu and Kashmir Police head constable Ashiq Hussain Qureshi at Anantnag's Lal Chowk while he was deployed on Amarnath Yatra duty. That attack, on July 22, was the first terror strike in Kashmir since the April 22, 2025 Pahalgam massacre, in which 26 people were killed.Friday's attack has also revived concerns over the safety of migrant workers in the Valley. In February 2024, two non-local labourers from Punjab, Amritpal Singh and Rohit Masih, were shot dead in Srinagar. Before that, in October 2021, terrorists killed two workers from Bihar, Raja Reshi Dev and Joginder Reshi Dev, in Kulgam's Wanpoh area.Lieutenant governor Manoj Sinha condemned the latest attack and said security forces had been instructed to intensify anti-terror operations."I strongly condemn this cowardly act. I have directed our security forces to step up their operations and eliminate the terrorists," Sinha wrote on X, adding that he had spoken to DGP Nalin Prabhat and other senior security officials.PDP president and former chief minister Mehbooba Mufti also condemned the killings."They work themselves to the bone far away from home only to feed their families. Unimaginably cruel to target them in such senseless acts of violence," she said.BJP's Jammu and Kashmir spokesperson Altaf Thakur described the attack as "cowardly, barbaric and inhuman", alleging that its objective was to disturb peace and normalcy in the Union Territory.The attack occurred during the ongoing Amarnath Yatra, which began on July 3. While the pilgrimage through the Pahalgam route has remained suspended since July 19 because of heavy rain and landslides, the Baltal route in Ganderbal continues to remain operational.Following the attack, security forces launched a cordon-and-search operation in the area to trace those responsible.
Article Summary: The attack took place late Friday night in the Kelam area of south Kashmir. One of the labourers, identified as Deepak Ratray, died before he could be shifted to a hospital. The second victim, Bopinder, was initially admitted to Government Medical College before being referred to SKIMS Hospital in Soura.

Article Title: J&K CM Omar Abdullah announces Rs 10 lakh aid after Kulgam terror attack kills two labourers
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Jammu and Kashmir chief minister Omar Abdullah on Saturday announced an ex gratia payment of Rs 10 lakh each for the families of two migrant labourers from Chhattisgarh who were killed in a terrorist attack at a brick kiln in Kulgam district.The attack took place late on Friday evening in the Kelam area of south Kashmir, where unidentified gunmen opened fire on the workers. The victims, both in their 20s, had travelled to the Valley in search of work after leaving their villages in Chhattisgarh.One of the labourers, 24-year-old Deepak Ratre, died before he could be taken to hospital. The second victim, 28-year-old Bhupendra Bhaina, was initially admitted to Government Medical College, Anantnag, before being shifted to SKIMS Hospital in Srinagar, where he later succumbed to his injuries.Deepak, from Bundeli village in Sakti district, was the sole breadwinner for his family, which includes his elderly mother, a physically disabled younger brother, his wife and their four-month-old son. His uncle said Deepak had moved to Jammu and Kashmir around seven to eight months ago with his wife to work at the brick kiln in the hope of building a better future.Bhupendra, from Chhuiya village in Sarangarh-Bilaigarh district, had reached Kashmir around three months ago with his wife.The couple had left their four-year-old son in the care of his grandmother and younger sister while other family members worked as labourers in Himachal Pradesh.Chhattisgarh chief minister Vishnu Deo Sai expressed grief over the killings, describing the attack as "cowardly". He said the state government stood firmly with the bereaved families and had directed officials to coordinate with the Jammu and Kashmir administration to bring the bodies back home.
Article Summary: The attack took place late on Friday evening in the Kelam area of south Kashmir. The victims, both in their 20s, had travelled to the Valley in search of work. One of the labourers, 24-year-old Deepak Ratre, died before he could be taken to hospital.

Article Title: Fear stalks Kashmir’s brick kilns after terrorists kill 2 migrant workers
Article Text:

KULGAM: Panic. Shuttered doors. Phones ringing with anxious calls from home. Brick kilns across south Kashmir ground to a halt Saturday as migrant labourers stayed indoors, rattled by the killing of two co-workers barely 2km away and wondering if they should leave — or stay and earn.Around 11am, Sunil Kumar, 34, and fellow labourer Renku Yadav stepped out of brick kiln No 515 in Hablishi village of Kulgam district to buy atta and pulses after running out of food. They had barely walked a short distance when the kiln owner chased after them, urging them to return.Fear had settled over the village after terrorists fatally shot two migrant labourers Friday evening at a brick kiln in neighbouring Kilam — killing Deepak Ratrey, 24, and Bhupendra Bhaina, 28, from Chhattisgarh.The attack raised concerns about the resurgence of targeted killings of non-native people in Kashmir. In 2022, a series of targeted attacks resulted in the deaths of at least 10 labourers.Terrorists tend to target “soft targets” such as migrant workers, who arrive in Kashmir every year between March and Nov — the seasonal workforce engaged in labour-intensive tasks on farms, construction sites and brick kilns.Kumar lives beside the kiln in a shelter built by stacking bricks without cement.The temporary rooms become home during the brick-making season.He has worked in J&K since 2007 and has spent nearly a decade at the same kiln, moulding clay bricks before they are fired. “Life has been peaceful in recent years. We work during the day, cook in the evening, listen to songs and speak to our families,” Kumar said.“We have seen such attacks in Kashmir, but what can a labourer do? We have to earn a living,” said Kumar, who came from Lucknow on July 16 with 12 more men for a monthly wage of Rs 18,000.Brick kiln owners fear a repeat of earlier years when attacks on migrant workers triggered an exodus, crippling businesses dependent on seasonal labour. “We came here for three months. We don’t think the situation is so bad that we should leave immediately,” Kumar assured.Zakir Ansari, 23, from Bareilly said he and nine men reached Kashmir in early July through a contractor. “Our family called all night worried, but we told them we were fine,” he said, adding that security personnel visited and assured their safety.Lt governor Manoj Sinha chaired a security review and directed officials to protect migrant workers. CM Omar Abdullah condemned the killings and announced Rs 10 lakh each for the victims’ families, in addition to Rs 6 lakh being provided by district administration.Political ripples followed the killings. NC president Dr Farooq Abdullah questioned why such attacks surface whenever the demand for restoration of J&K’s statehood gathers momentum, drawing sharp criticism from BJP and PDP. BJP’s Sunil Sharma called the remarks “very strange”, while PDP functionary Iltija Mufti urged that “a moment of grief shouldn’t be politicised”.
Article Summary: Terrorists killed two migrant labourers Friday evening at a brick kiln in neighbouring Kilam. The attack raised concerns about the resurgence of targeted killings of non-native people in Kashmir. In 2022, a series of targeted attacks resulted in the deaths of at least 10 labourers.

NEW DELHI: The family of one of the two Chhattisgarh labourers killed in the terror attack in Jammu and Kashmir's Kulgam has alleged that the attackers asked the victims about their identity and religion before opening fire, echoing survivor accounts from the April 2025 Pahalgam terror attack.Deepak Ratrey, a resident of Bundeli village in Chhattisgarh's Sakti district, was among two migrant labourers killed when terrorists attacked a brick kiln in Kulgam on Friday night. Another victim was identified as 28-year-old Bhupendra Bhaina from Sarangarh-Bilaigarh district. Both had travelled to Kashmir in search of work and were employed at the brick kiln where the attack took place.Speaking to ANI, Deepak's uncle Haldhar Ratrey claimed the attackers targeted the labourers after asking about their identity. "From what we've heard, the terrorists shot him after asking about his caste and community. Look at this act by the terrorists - they went and shot him after asking his caste, firing at a labourer," he alleged.While there has been no official confirmation on this from the authorities, Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge , in a post on X, also said the two labourers were "identified" before they were killed, which reflected the "cruel mindset of terrorism."The incident comes days after terrorists shot dead Jammu and Kashmir Police head constable Ashiq Hussain Qureshi in Anantnag while he was deployed on Amarnath Yatra duty. It was the first terror strike in Kashmir since the April 22, 2025 Pahalgam terror attack, in which 26 people were killed. Survivors of that attack had also alleged that terrorists asked victims about their religion before opening fire.Deepak had moved to Jammu and Kashmir about a year ago to work at a brick kiln and was the sole breadwinner for his family. He is survived by his wife, a one-year-old son, his widowed mother and a disabled brother.His family has appealed to the government to bring his mortal remains back to Chhattisgarh for the last rites and provide financial assistance to the bereaved family.Sakti sub-divisional magistrate Rupendra Patel said the administration was in constant touch with the family and coordinating with authorities in Jammu and Kashmir to ensure all possible assistance and expedite the transportation of Deepak's body to his native village.Jammu and Kashmir chief minister Omar Abdullah announced an ex gratia of Rs 10 lakh each for the families of the two victims. Chhattisgarh chief minister Vishnu Deo Sai also condemned the killings and directed officials to coordinate with the Jammu and Kashmir administration to facilitate the return of the bodies.Additionally, Chhattisgarh Deputy CM Vijay Sharma also said that victims family told him that terrorists conversed for 10 minutes before shootin. "I have also spoken to the relatives. They recounted that the terrorists arrived, sat and conversed for ten minutes, and only then opened fire. This is a cowardly act. No matter how much one might ponder it, every inch of Jammu & Kashmir belongs to India, and Indians will go there and live there.It is Indian soil; there should be no doubt about this. India will not be intimidated by such hollow threats. These terrorists will soon be hunted down and will meet the same fate as their predecessors," he said.Deepak, the sole breadwinner of his family, had moved to Jammu and Kashmir around seven to eight months ago with his wife. He is survived by his elderly mother, a physically disabled younger brother, his wife and their four-month-old son.Bhupendra had arrived in Kashmir about three months ago with his wife, while their four-year-old son remained in Chhattisgarh with relatives.
Article Summary: Family of one of the two Chhattisgarh labourers killed in the terror attack in Jammu and Kashmir's Kulgam has alleged that the attackers asked the victims about their identity and religion before opening fire. It was the first terror strike in Kashmir since the April 22, 2025 Pahalgam terror attack, in which 26 people were killed.

Article Title: Ladakh Police file zero FIR against influencer over alleged anti-Amit Shah Facebook video
Article Text:
According to the FIR, the complainant alleged that the video was likely to promote hostility and disturb public order and communal harmony

NEW DELHI: Ladakh Police on Saturday registered a zero FIR against social media influencer Yogesh Parmar over the circulation of a Facebook video that allegedly contains objectionable remarks targeting Union Home Minister Amit Shah , and transferred the case to Karnataka for further investigation, officials said.The FIR was lodged at Leh police station after a written complaint alleged that a Facebook video shared through a link contained remarks that were “highly objectionable, hateful and offensive” against the home minister.The case has been registered under Sections 197(1)(d) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) relating to acts against national integration, 352 for insult intended to provoke a breach of peace, and 353(1) for public mischief, officials said.The offences carry punishments ranging from two to three years of imprisonment, along with a fine, or both, depending on the specific provision.According to the FIR, the complainant alleged that the video was likely to promote hostility and disturb public order and communal harmony.“It is alleged that the content is likely to promote hostility, disturb public order and harmony by inciting resentment among the public.The allegations prima facie disclose the commission of a cognisable offence punishable under sections 197(1)(d), 352, 353(1) of the BNS,” officials said, citing the FIR.As the alleged incident falls under the jurisdiction of the Devaraja police station in Mysuru City, Karnataka, Leh police registered a zero FIR and transferred the case to the concerned police station for further investigation, officials added.A zero FIR allows police to register a cognisable offence irrespective of where the alleged incident took place and subsequently transfer the case to the appropriate jurisdiction.
Article Summary: The case has been registered under Sections 197(1)(d) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) relating to acts against national integration. The offences carry punishments ranging from two to three years of imprisonment, along with a fine, or both, depending on the specific provision.

Article Title: CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke falls sick again while meeting people in building parking
Article Text:
Dipke's father, Bhagwan Dipke, said doctors had been called to examine his son.

NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke fell ill again on Saturday morning after feeling uneasy and vomiting while meeting supporters at his residence in Maharashtra's Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, days after revealing that he had been diagnosed with typhoid.The incident occurred at around 11.45 am, when Dipke came down to the parking area of his residence to meet a group of people waiting to see him.According to those present, he suddenly felt unwell and moved to the rear of the building, where he vomited. He later returned upstairs to his residence without speaking to the media.Confirming the incident, Dipke's father, Bhagwan Dipke, said doctors had been called to examine his son.Dipke had disclosed on July 25, during the protests at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi, that he had been diagnosed with typhoid. At the time, he said he had been unwell for several days and was undergoing treatment.
Article Summary: Abhijeet Dipke fell ill again on Saturday morning after feeling uneasy and vomiting. Dipke had disclosed on July 25, during the protests at Jantar Mantar, that he had been diagnosed with typhoid. His father, Bhagwan Dipke, said doctors had been called to examine his son.

Article Title: Cloudburst damages structures in Kishtwar; rain halts Amarnath Yatra
Article Text: JAMMU: Flash floods triggered by a cloudburst in Chatroo area of J&K’s Kishtwar district early Saturday damaged shops and houses, inundated the main market with boulders, mud and slush, damaged Kishtwar–Chatroo–Sinthan national highway, and prompted authorities to shut schools.Meanwhile, Amarnath Yatra was suspended from Jammu’s Bhagwati Nagar base camp on Saturday as Jammu–Srinagar NH remained closed for the second consecutive day due to incessant rain.“At least two vehicles parked near a local stream in Kishtwar were washed away, while four to five shops and around three houses were damaged. No casualties have been reported so far,” an official said.Union minister Jitendra Singh said shopkeepers and business owners affected by the cloudburst would receive compensation in accordance with govt relief norms.Schools also remained shut in Doda, Poonch, and Ramban districts due to incessant rain.
Article Summary: Flash floods triggered by a cloudburst in Chatroo area of J&K’s Kishtwar district. Floods inundated the main market with boulders, mud and slush. No casualties have been reported so far, an official said.

Article Title: ‘My return to Kolkata proves injustice cannot be permanent’: Taslima Nasreen
Article Text:
Exiled Bangladeshi author Taslima Nasreen in Kolkata. (PTI Photo)

NEW DELHI: Exiled Bangladeshi author Taslima Nasreen on Saturday described her return to India after nearly two decades as proof that “injustice can be long but cannot be permanent. ”She made the remarks at an event in Kolkata, nearly two decades after she was forced to leave the city in 2007. The 63-year-old writer had been living in Kolkata since leaving Bangladesh in 1994 amid alleged death threats from radical groups over her writings and views on religion.Nasreen, who has been living in Europe since leaving Kolkata, also clarified that her return to the city was not linked to any "political agenda.""Today, the opening of this door proves that injustice can be long, but it cannot be permanent. History remembers who closed the doors and who opened them...I am not here to speak for any political party, or against any party. I am here to speak in favour of women's rights," PTI quoted her as saying.She also expressed concern over what she described as a "rise" in religious extremism in Bangladesh."I am against all forms of fundamentalism, but I have spoken against Islamic fundamentalists because I have seen it from close quarters since childhood.The rise of fundamentalism in Bangladesh is at an alarming stage. Freedom of speech is being curtailed," Nasreen said.Visibly emotional, Nasreen called her return a "fulfilment of a long-awaited moment.""It took me 19 years to say these words: 'I have returned to Kolkata.' I felt the pain of losing an address every single day. On August 8, 1994, the then government forced me to leave Bangladesh. The state may have removed me from my country, but it could never remove my country from within me," she added.Lamenting that she could not find a permanent home in either Bangladesh or West Bengal, Nasreen highlighted that Europe had provided her security but not a sense of belonging."Europe has given me citizenship and a place to live, but unfortunately, I couldn't get a small place to stay in the two Bengals. Europe gave me security, but it could not give me a sense of belonging. A home is not built by security alone; it is built by language, memory and culture," Nasreen remarked.Nasreen maintained that she had never been convicted by any court but had faced restrictions because of opposition from fundamentalist groups."I committed no crime. No court has ever punished me. It is a painful truth of our times that a writer needs police protection to visit the city of her own language."Rejecting allegations that her writings were offensive, she emphasised that her advocacy had focused on equality and human rights."I only spoke about equal rights for women and men, and about human rights irrespective of religion or caste. I said that any rule or doctrine that takes away equality and human dignity must be changed."She also criticised what she described as the unequal treatment of women in the name of religion and backed a Uniform Civil Code across South Asia, arguing that religion-based personal laws discriminate against women."The real conflict is between secularism and fundamentalism, between the rational mind and irrationality, between innovation and tradition, and between people who value freedom and those who do not."
Article Summary: Taslima Nasreen was forced to leave Kolkata in 1994 amid alleged death threats. The 63-year-old writer had been living in Europe since leaving the city in 2007. Nasreen said her return to the city was not linked to any "political agenda"

NEW DELHI: Congress ' internal rift in Punjab showed no signs of easing on Saturday after supporters of former chief minister Charanjit Singh Channi disrupted two party programmes by raising slogans in his favour, prompting AICC general secretary in charge of Punjab Bhupesh Baghel to warn that anyone indulging in indiscipline would be expelled from the party.The slogan shouting took place during the Congress' 'Har Booth, Congress Mazboot' programmes in Patiala and Sangrur, where Baghel, Punjab Congress chief Amarinder Singh Raja Warring and several senior leaders were present.Despite the disruption, Baghel reiterated that the Congress high command would decide the party's chief ministerial face only after the Punjab Assembly elections, due early next year.The disruption began in Patiala soon after Warring started addressing party workers. Channi's supporters raised slogans including "Charanjit Singh Channi Zindabad", "Channi Teri Soch Te Pehra Deyange Thok Ke" and "Channi Liyao, Punjab Bachao", briefly bringing the programme to a halt.A visibly upset Warring repeatedly appealed to workers to maintain discipline and allow the meeting to continue but the slogan shouting persisted for some time before proceedings resumed.Senior Congress leaders, including Baghel, MP Amar Singh and Brahm Mohindra, witnessed the developments while other leaders attempted to calm the workers.Similar scenes unfolded later in Sangrur, where another group of Channi supporters raised slogans in favour of the former chief minister and against Baghel. Tensions escalated after some of Channi's supporters clashed verbally with other Congress workers.One supporter demanded that the Jalandhar MP be declared the Congress' chief ministerial face, claiming it reflected the wishes of party workers.However, Warring dismissed suggestions that Channi had orchestrated the protests."Channi did not send these people. He is our crown," Warring said in Sangrur, while alleging that the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) had sent people to disrupt the Congress programme.Addressing party workers, Baghel urged leaders to remain united and focus on defeating the ruling AAP, the BJP and the Shiromani Akali Dal instead of engaging in internal rivalries.He made it clear that the Congress leadership, including party president Mallikarjun Kharge and leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi, would decide the chief ministerial candidate and ministers only after the Assembly elections."Smaller differences are part of every party which can be sorted out for the bigger battle that the Congress has to fight against AAP, BJP and Akalis," Baghel said.He expressed confidence that the Congress would emerge stronger in the Assembly elections because everyone shared the common objective of bringing the party back to power in Punjab.Baghel also underlined the importance of strengthening the party at the booth level, saying a strong grassroots organisation would be key to electoral success.Later, speaking to reporters in Patiala, Baghel issued a stern warning against indiscipline."Whosoever indulges in indiscipline will be shown the door from the party irrespective of the position one holds," he said, citing the earlier expulsion of Navjot Kaur Sidhu as an example.When asked whether the party would initiate action against Channi, Baghel responded by asking what mistake the former chief minister had committed.Warring, meanwhile, announced that former MLA Madan Lal Jalalpur had been suspended for remarks against senior Congress leaders.Rejecting reports that some leaders had stayed away from district committee meetings, Baghel said all leaders had been informed about the programmes and were participating as their schedules permitted.In his address, Warring stressed that no leader, regardless of popularity, could win elections without a strong organisational structure.He cited the example of late Punjabi singer Sidhu Moosewala, saying that despite his immense popularity, he lost the 2022 Assembly election by over 60,000 votes because of inadequate booth-level management.Warring also said his only wish was to see a Congress chief minister and ministers taking oath after the next Assembly elections, adding that he would be happy to watch the swearing-in ceremony from the audience.He described senior leaders including Channi, Partap Singh Bajwa, Rajinder Kaur Bhattal and Brahm Mohindra as more experienced and capable than himself, and assured workers that all senior leaders would soon be seen sharing one platform ahead of the polls.The latest developments indicate continuing factionalism within the Punjab Congress despite repeated assurances from the party leadership that organisational unity is being strengthened ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections.Baghel is currently touring the poll-bound state as part of the 'Har Booth, Congress Mazboot' campaign, meeting district and block-level leaders after launching the initiative in Fatehgarh Sahib and Mohali on Friday.Baghel had earlier dismissed reports of factionalism, claiming that the media and a few individuals were creating a perception of infighting.However, discontent within the state unit has continued since the Congress retained Amarinder Singh Raja Warring as Punjab Congress president while appointing Channi as chairman of the campaign committee.A section of leaders led by Channi and Sukhjinder Singh Randhawa had opposed Warring's continuation as state chief and sought his removal.
Article Summary: Channi supporters disrupt Congress meetings in Patiala and Sangrur. AICC general secretary in charge of Punjab Bhupesh Baghel warns against indiscipline. Baghel says the party's chief ministerial face will be decided after polls.

Article Title: DMK moves SC seeking immediate release of Cauvery water from Karnataka to Tamil Nadu
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) on Saturday moved the Supreme Court seeking directions to the Karnataka government to immediately release Cauvery water to Tamil Nadu, arguing that Karnataka must comply with the apex court's 2018 verdict and the recent directions issued by the Cauvery Water Management Authority (CWMA).The plea seeks an order directing Karnataka to implement the Cauvery Water Regulation Committee's recommendation, upheld by the CWMA on Thursday, to release 3,500 cusecs of water per day for 15 days to Tamil Nadu at the inter-state border point of Biligundlu."Direct the State of Karnataka / Respondent No. 1 to forthwith and fully implement the direction of the CWRC dated July 28, 2026, as affirmed by the CWMA on July 30, 2026, by ensuring a flow of 3,500 cusecs per day at Biligundlu for the period of 15 days commencing from date of the order passed by this Hon'ble Court, and to make good the shortfall in compliance from July 29, 2026 onwards," the DMK said in its plea.The party also sought a direction to Karnataka to clear the accumulated shortfall in water releases. It asked the court to direct the state to "make good the accumulated backlog of about 9.46 TMC due at Biligundlu as on July 26, 2026, computed on the pro-rata/distress-sharing basis, by ensuring releases such that about 7,000 cusecs per day is realised at Biligundlu over a period of 15 days".In addition, the DMK urged the Supreme Court to direct the CWMA to monitor reservoir releases in Karnataka and the flows realised at Biligundlu on a day-to-day basis and submit compliance reports.The move comes amid renewed tensions between the two southern states over the sharing of Cauvery waters during the current monsoon season. On Thursday, the CWMA upheld the Cauvery Water Regulation Committee's recommendation that Karnataka release 3,500 cusecs of water daily for the next 15 days to Tamil Nadu.Responding to the growing protests in Karnataka, chief minister DK Shivakumar appealed on Saturday to organisations opposing the release of water to withdraw their proposed agitation. The farmer groups and pro-Kannada organisations staged demonstrations across the Cauvery basin, arguing that the state could not spare even a drop of water for Tamil Nadu because major reservoirs did not have enough water even for drinking.Shivakumar said the Kabini reservoir was rapidly filling up and warned that water could not be retained once the reservoir reached full capacity."Kabini reservoir is filling up. Once a dam is full, water has to be released. It is impossible to hold it back. I humbly appeal to those planning to agitate against the release of water to withdraw their decision," he said.Shivakumar also cautioned protesters against approaching water release points, saying, "Even if we decide not to release water, once the reservoir is full, it is impossible to hold it back. Protesters should not go near the points where water is being released. The force of the water can sweep you away. No one should lie down in the path of flowing water."The Karnataka CM said the state would protect the interests of its farmers while respecting judicial orders. "There is an order to release 177 TMC of water to Tamil Nadu, and the Supreme Court has upheld it. We must respect the court's order while also protecting the interests of our farmers. Our government is committed to safeguarding the welfare of Karnataka's farmers," he said.He also accused the BJP of "politicising" the issue and said an all-party meeting would be held to consult former chief ministers, political leaders and legal experts before deciding the state's next course of action. According to Shivakumar, Tamil Nadu had sought 9,000 cusecs, but the Authority had directed Karnataka to release only 3,500 cusecs.The Cauvery Water Management Authority was constituted by the Centre in 2018 following the Supreme Court's final verdict on the decades-old Cauvery river water dispute among Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Kerala and Puducherry. The Authority includes representatives of the riparian states as well as a nominee of the central government and is responsible for overseeing implementation of the court-mandated water-sharing arrangement.
Article Summary: The Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) on Saturday moved the Supreme Court seeking directions to the Karnataka government to immediately release Cauvery water to Tamil Nadu. The party argues that Karnataka must comply with the apex court's 2018 verdict and the recent directions issued by the Cauved Water Management Authority. The move comes amid renewed tensions between the two southern states over the sharing of Cauvey waters.

NEW DELHI: BJP's West Bengal unit president Samik Bhattacharya on Saturday cautioned party workers against becoming arrogant, warning that the infamous "egg therapy" could otherwise "turn on its head. Everyone, including those in my party, must understand that. Those ‘Sanatanis’ who have suddenly found a place in our party and are harbouring aspirations for influence and advantage must also remain careful because the trajectory of those eggs can change in no time,” the Rajya Sabha MP remarked, apparently referring to leaders who joined the BJP from the Trinamool Congress (TMC), which lost power in West Bengal after 15 years.The “egg therapy” Bhattacharya mentioned alluded to incidents of egg-pelting targeting TMC leaders after the party's defeat.He also acknowledged that despite having assumed political power in West Bengal, the BJP has not yet been entirely successful in eradicating the "culture of extortion.""Our government has come to power only two months ago. We have not been able to solve all problems. If I say that we have been able to eradicate extortion from everywhere, then I will be making a false claim.There are deviations. People had become accustomed to passing through a system of making easy money through syndicates. Not everything has changed with the change in state power," Bhattacharya told the audience."Some joined the ruling party (BJP) within four hours, others had dormant wishes that have now surfaced. We are trying to control such tendencies within the party. Our CM Suvendu Adhikari is also trying to apply strict brakes on such tendencies."Emphasising the need to free the business ecosystem from "partisan politics," the BJP leader argued that West Bengal stood at the "cusp of breaking with its chequered industrial past.""We must keep partisan politics out of this system. We have become residents of a political society in West Bengal. We need freedom from it. Article Title: India’s students do not need PM Modi's forgiveness, they are owed his apology: Rahul Gandhi

Behind every young life lost is a family carrying pain that will never leave them - and serious questions about a broken education system,” Gandhi said in a post on X where he also shared images of his interaction with parents and students.“Leaked papers. Cancelled exams. Years of preparation destroyed overnight. Our students are told to work honestly in a system that is not honest with them. And the Prime Minister has the audacity to speak of “forgiving” students,” Gandhi added.Alleging that the PM has not met a single grieving parent and has not sat with a single student whose future was stolen by a leaked paper, Gandhi said that the students don’t need Modi’s forgiveness rather “they are owed his apology”.Reacting sharply to the PM”s video, Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh said in a post on X that the “PM enjoys playing the victim card” and added that Modi’s “InstaGram Sabhas are fooling no one”.“Late last night, in an act of supreme self-obsession, the PM said that he forgave our youth. Article Summary: Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi lashed out at the PM for having the "audacity" to speak of "forgiving" students. "India’s students do not need his forgiveness. Article Title: 'Whenever we seek statehood': Farooq Abdullah questions 'timing' of Kulgam terror attack

NEW DELHI: National Conference (NC) president Farooq Abdullah on Saturday questioned the timing of the terrorist attack on two migrant labourers in Kulgam, asking why such incidents occur whenever his party demands the restoration of statehood for Jammu and Kashmir.The NC had staged a protest in Delhi on July 20, demanding the restoration of statehood for Jammu and Kashmir.“I regret it. We do not even know who killed them or how they were killed. There should be an investigation, a fair probe to identify those responsible,” Abdullah told reporters in north Kashmir's Baramulla district, according to PTI.“I don’t know why such incidents happen whenever we seek statehood,” the former Jammu and Kashmir chief minister added.Deepak Ratray and Bopinder, both in their 20s and from Chhattisgarh, were killed in a terrorist attack at a brick kiln in the Kelam area of south Kashmir's Kulgam district late on Friday evening.Officials said Ratray died before he could be taken to a hospital, while Bopinder succumbed to his injuries during treatment.The attack came days after Jammu and Kashmir Police head constable Ashiq Hussain was shot dead by a lone terrorist in Anantnag's Lal Chowk area while on Amarnath Yatra duty on July 22.On August 5, 2019, the Narendra Modi-led Centre revoked Article 370, which granted special status to Jammu and Kashmir. Two months later, in October 2019, the-then state was bifurcated into the Union territories of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh.Farooq Abdullah's son, Omar Abdullah, became the first chief minister of the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir after taking office in October 2024.Meanwhile, People's Democratic Party (PDP) chief and former chief minister Mehbooba Mufti termed the killing of the two non-local workers a "security lapse" and sought a high-level investigation into the attack."People come here to work as labourers... Why do they travel so far? Because, perhaps, there is no employment for them back home. They find work here in Kashmir, yet they are being gunned down like this. I have no words to condemn this incident," Mufti said in Srinagar."I believe there is a lapse in security somewhere. I request that the local government should provide compensation to these victims, in addition to whatever compensation their home state provides. A proper investigation must be conducted... The government needs to examine where the lapses are occurring—how militants managed to come in and kill two unarmed individuals despite the presence of the Army, CRPF and police," she added.
Article Summary: National Conference president Farooq Abdullah questions timing of terrorist attack. Two migrant labourers were killed in a terrorist attack at a brick kiln in south Kashmir. PDP chief and former chief minister Mehbooba Mufti alleges security lapse.

NEW DELHI: National Security Advisor (NSA) Ajit Doval on Saturday received the Lokmanya Tilak National Award in Pune in recognition of his contribution to strengthening India's national security.Union home minister Amit Shah presented the award at a ceremony held on the 106th death anniversary of freedom fighter Lokmanya Bal Gangadhar Tilak.The event took place at the Kataria High School ground in Mukundnagar and was attended by Maharashtra chief minister Devendra Fadnavis, deputy chief ministers Eknath Shinde and Sunetra Pawar, along with several senior political leaders and dignitaries.The award, presented by the Lokmanya Tilak Smarak Trust, honours individuals for their outstanding contribution to the nation. Trust president Rohit Tilak had earlier announced that Doval was chosen this year for his role in strengthening India's national security.Doval, the country's longest-serving National Security Advisor, has played a key role in shaping India's security strategy and has been associated with several major operations, including Operation Sindoor, the Balakot air strike and the surgical strikes .Instituted in 1983, the Lokmanya Tilak National Award has previously been conferred on several eminent personalities. Veteran socialist S M Joshi was the first recipient of the honour. Former President Pranab Mukherjee, Prime Ministers Narendra Modi, Atal Bihari Vajpayee and Manmohan Singh are among the distinguished recipients. Union minister Nitin Gadkari received the award last year.
Article Summary: Ajit Doval is the country's longest-serving National Security Advisor. He has played a key role in shaping India's security strategy. Doval has been associated with several major operations, including Operation Sindoor. The Lokmanya Tilak National Award honours individuals for their outstanding contribution to the nation.

Article Title: Delhi riots 2020: Why Tahir Hussain escaped death penalty in IB officer Ankit Sharma murder case
Article Text:
Why the court awarded life imprisonment instead of death

Prosecution sought death penalty

Court's conviction order

Murder during Delhi riots

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: A Delhi court on Friday sentenced former AAP councillor Tahir Hussain and four others to life imprisonment for the murder of Intelligence Bureau (IB) officer Ankit Sharma during the 2020 northeast Delhi riots, rejecting the prosecution's plea for the death penalty after holding that it had failed to prove the convicts were beyond the possibility of reformation.Additional Sessions Judge Praveen Singh pronounced the sentence after hearing arguments from both the prosecution and the defence on the quantum of punishment. The court said the prosecution had not established that the case met the threshold for awarding capital punishment, even though it had convicted Hussain and four others for Sharma's murder earlier this month.The judgment was delivered in the physical presence of Hussain and the other convicts amid tight security at Delhi's Karkardooma Court.While the Delhi Police had argued that the case fell within the "rarest of rare" category warranting capital punishment, the court concluded that the prosecution had not proved that the convicts were incapable of reform, a key principle laid down by the Supreme Court for awarding the death penalty.Additional Sessions Judge Praveen Singh observed that the prosecution was unable to establish that the convicts were beyond reformation, leading the court to impose life imprisonment instead.The prosecution had sought the death penalty for Hussain and the four co-convicts, arguing that the murder was brutal, deliberate and carried out without any provocation.During the sentencing hearing, Special Public Prosecutor Madhukar Pandey described the crime as "anti-social and abhorrent" and argued that it qualified as one of the "rarest of rare" cases.Pandey told the court that Sharma was subjected to a cold-blooded and savage attack with a heavy cutting weapon and that the killing could not be viewed in isolation because it occurred during the northeast Delhi riots in which 53 people lost their lives.According to the prosecution, Sharma sustained 51 injuries, seven of which were independently sufficient to cause death.The prosecution further submitted that the convicts acted without provocation and displayed complete disregard for the consequences of their actions.Earlier, Pandey had argued that the accused had fallen to the "level of being animals" while assaulting Sharma and said:"Those who are asking for mercy today should have shown mercy themselves. No mercy was shown from anyone's side. No one even took Ankit to the hospital. They are asking for mercy after committing such a brutal murder."The prosecution also argued that Hussain, being an elected municipal councillor at the time, had a greater responsibility to protect citizens instead of becoming part of the unlawful assembly.The defence, however, urged the court to show leniency, arguing that not every murder warranted capital punishment and that aggravating and mitigating circumstances must both be considered.Senior advocate Rajiv Mohan, appearing for Hussain, argued that six of the eleven accused in the case had already been acquitted and that the prosecution had failed to establish any conspiracy during the trial.The defence maintained that Hussain's conviction rested on his membership of an unlawful assembly and common intention rather than evidence showing he personally inflicted fatal injuries on Sharma.The counsel further argued that there had been no preparation or conspiracy, that Sharma had been attacked by a large crowd during widespread rioting and that Hussain's conduct during custody had remained satisfactory.Advocate Tara Narula also urged the court to consider Hussain's family circumstances, submitting that he had three children, an elderly father and that his wife was a homemaker dependent on rental income.Counsel representing the other convicts similarly pleaded for leniency, citing their family responsibilities and arguing that both communities had been involved in the violence.The court, however, rejected several of the defence's contentions before pronouncing the sentence.On July 13, the court convicted Hussain and four others for Sharma's murder.In its conviction order, the court held that Hussain was a member of a heavily armed mob that had assembled with animus against Hindus to commit rioting, arson and looting before murdering Sharma in what it described as a "savage and relentless assault."The court further held that the prosecution had proved members of the unlawful assembly knew that pursuing their common object could result in death.Ankit Sharma, an Intelligence Bureau officer, was killed during the northeast Delhi riots in February 2020 in the Dayalpur area. His mutilated body was later recovered from a drain.Hussain was convicted under Sections 302 (murder), 365 (kidnapping or abducting with intent secretly and wrongfully to confine a person), 147 (rioting), 148 (rioting armed with a deadly weapon), 153A (promoting enmity) and 188 (disobedience to an order duly promulgated by a public servant) of the Indian Penal Code, read with Section 149 relating to unlawful assembly.With Friday's sentencing order, Hussain and the four co-convicts will serve life imprisonment, while the court's decision underscores that despite the brutality of the crime, the legal threshold required for imposing the death penalty was not met because the prosecution failed to prove they were beyond the possibility of reformation.
Article Summary: A Delhi court sentenced former AAP councillor Tahir Hussain and four others to life imprisonment for the murder of Intelligence Bureau (IB) officer Ankit Sharma during the 2020 northeast Delhi riots. The court rejected the prosecution's plea for the death penalty after holding that it had failed to prove the convicts were beyond the possibility of reformation.

NEW DELHI: AAP turncoat and BJP MP Raghav Chadha on Thursday broke his prolonged silence on the paper leak issue, speaking for the first time from the ruling side in Rajya Sabha. As BJP pushed the anti-paper leak Bill in the Parliament, Chadha said he did not want headlines but spoke "wholeheartedly in support of the students of India," adding that "PM Modi heard it just like the head of a family listens. Historic decisions taken. System changed," Chadha said.He also said that the government "heard and delivered."Highlighting the impact of paper leaks on students, he added, "Because a paper leak does not merely compromise an examination. It can wipe out years of preparation in a single moment."He further said, "Every student deserves an examination system where hard work and merit, not a leaked paper, decide the result."Months ago, Chadha led a rebel exodus from Arvind Kejriwal-founded AAP, with seven Rajya Sabha members from the party breaking away and merging their faction with the ruling BJP.However, the Bill came under sharp criticism from the Opposition in the Rajya Sabha. Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge led the attack after Union minister Jitendra Singh tabled the Bill in the Upper House.Parliament Thursday approved the Public Examination (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026, introducing stricter penalties for paper leaks and exam-related malpractices. The government said the legislation addresses one of the biggest concerns affecting students and called for cooperation from all stakeholders to tackle the issue.The Bill was passed by a voice vote in the Rajya Sabha amid an opposition walkout, a day after it cleared the Lok Sabha.Under the amended law, individuals found guilty of paper leaks or other unfair means in public examinations will face a minimum prison term of five years, extendable to 10 years, along with a fine of up to Rs 50 lakh.For organised exam-related crimes, the Bill prescribes a minimum jail term of seven years and a fine of up to Rs 10 crore.The legislation also empowers state governments and Union Territory administrations to designate Courts of Session as special fast-track courts to try offences under the Act. These courts will conduct day-to-day proceedings and complete trials within three months of the filing of the chargesheet.The Bill further authorises the central government to constitute a special task force to investigate offences under the Act whenever necessary.

Article Title: Singapore student Siti Aishah Siregar left home saying she was going to college; hours later her family found her passport missing and a Cambodia flight ticket in her email
Article Text:

Singapore student Siti Aishah Siregar left home saying she was going to college; hours later her family found her passport missing and a Cambodia flight ticket in her email.Singapore police confirmed that the 20-year-old had already left the country on an outbound flight, prompting an urgent search to track her down in Phnom Penh.According to the teenager's eldest brother, Syafiq Siregar, who spoke to news outlet Berita Mediacorp, Aishah informed her mother at around 11am on 28 July that she was travelling to Nanyang Polytechnic as usual.Concerns grew later that afternoon when family members arrived at the college campus at about 5pm to pick her up. They discovered that her mobile phone was completely unreachable and her WhatsApp account had been deactivated.Upon returning home, the family noticed that Aishah's passport was missing from the house. After logging into her email account, they uncovered a flight ticket booking confirmation bound for Phnom Penh, Cambodia.Her father, Sahat Siregar, issued an emotional appeal on Facebook on 30 July, begging authorities in both Singapore and Cambodia for immediate assistance to locate his daughter.He wrote that his daughter is believed to be in Phnom Penh and appealed directly to officials and members of the public to "bring Aishah back home".In his post, he asked authorities to "please help us find my daughter as soon as possible".The family confirmed they have lodged a formal police report in Singapore and are working closely with law enforcement. Expressing the family's growing anxiety, the father highlighted that every moment counts."We are afraid that every hour we lose could make it harder to bring her home safely," he wrote in the post, adding, "As a father, I am begging for your help. I just want my daughter to come home safe."In his appeal, Sahat thanked those who had assisted the family and requested that people share his message widely across social media, noting that "someone may have seen something or know something that could help"."If you have any information, no matter how small, please contact me or the Singapore police immediately," he wrote. "Please keep my daughter in your prayers. Please help bring my daughter home safely."

Article Title: Mushroom hunters entered a Nepal forest and found a nest built by the only snake known to make one. Officials have now restricted access while conservationists monitor the site
Article Text:
The discovery has prompted authorities to limit public access to the region while conservationists monitor the nesting site.

A curious discovery

The only snake that builds a nest

Why king cobras matter

In a routine search for wild mushrooms deep in a community forest in Nepal, extraordinary wildlife has been discovered. Local residents exploring the forest floor near Jhakri Sota in the Ambe Community Forest came across something few people ever get to see: a carefully built nest of a king cobra. For the uninitiated, the king cobra is one of the world’s most elusive reptiles, but it’s also the only known snake to build nests for its eggs. The discovery has prompted authorities to limit public access to the region while conservationists monitor the nesting site.According to a news report by The Cool Down website, the nest was found on July 15 by members of the Ambe Community Forest while they were collecting mushrooms in Ghorahi Sub-Metropolitan City, Nepal. Recognising the importance of the find, the community immediately alerted local conservationists. With the help of snake rescuer and conservationist Kuldeep Neupane, who has been doing snake rescue and awareness in the region for the last four years, the area was secured quickly to minimize disturbance to the nesting female. The report also states that officials have temporarily closed off the forest around it to protect people and wildlife.Local residents have been told not to collect mushrooms, firewood or grass near the nesting site until the eggs hatch and the cobra departs naturally. The Division Forest Office has also increased surveillance and is working in close coordination with the community forest users committee to ensure the area remains undisturbed during this crucial breeding period.According to experts, the female king cobra collects dry leaves, twigs and other forest vegetation to build a nest, a behavior not seen in any other known snake. The female lays 30-40 eggs and stays in the vicinity to protect the nest until the eggs hatch in roughly two to three months. Such an exceptional degree of parental care makes the species especially vulnerable to human disturbance during the breeding season. Then there’s the king cobra, the world’s longest venomous snake, measuring more than 18 feet (5.5 metres) long, which adds to its mystique.Unlike most snakes, they mostly eat other snakes, including venomous snakes. This helps them control snake populations, which helps maintain ecological balance, and may even reduce the chances of humans coming into contact with other dangerous snakes. It is believed that a decline in king cobra populations could upset this balance, Thus this finding serves as an important reminder that apex predators, although feared by many, often provide vital ecological services.Where human lives and wildlife collideThe incident also underscores an increasing problem across much of Asia: expanding encroachment of human activity into habitat of the wild. Community forests frequently contribute to rural livelihoods through access to mushrooms, medicinal plants, firewood and fodder. Meanwhile, these forests remain critical habitats for a multitude of wild species. The presence of a nesting king cobra in an area that is frequented by local residents is obviously a safety concern, especially considering that female king cobras are extremely defensive when guarding their eggs. It is reported that instead of pulling the snake out, authorities are taking a more balanced approach – temporarily limiting human activity while letting nature take its course and it is an example of coexistence through caution rather than conflict.Enhancing conservation initiativesThe discovery has also revived debates on wildlife protection in Nepal. While the king cobra is internationally classified as a Vulnerable species, conservationists point out that it is not currently listed among Nepal's protected wildlife species. The remarkable find could fuel calls for stronger legal protections and habitat conservation.
Article Summary: The nest was found on July 15 by members of the Ambe Community Forest in Ghorahi Sub-Metropolitan City, Nepal. The discovery has prompted authorities to limit public access to the region while conservationists monitor the nesting site. The female king cobra lays 30-40 eggs and stays in the vicinity to protect the nest until the eggs hatch in roughly two to three months.

Article Title: Gurgaon MNC employee dies by suicide, son records video as mother screams for help
Article Text:
A Gurugram man was found hanging after his wife sought a divorce. His seven-year-old son reportedly recorded a video of the incident





GURGAON: A 36-year-old associate operator at a multinational company was found hanging at his home in Gurgaon's Surat Nagar, with police investigating allegations by his family that marital discord may have preceded his death.The deceased, identified as Sanjeev Yadav, allegedly died by suicide on Thursday while only his wife, Manpreet Kaur, and their seven-year-old son were at home. Police said the child is believed to have recorded a video on a mobile phone showing his father hanging, while his mother was heard shouting for help.According to police, Manpreet immediately informed both her family and Sanjeev's relatives after discovering him hanging.Sanjeev's sister, Kiran, alleged that her brother had been under stress as his wife was seeking a divorce. She claimed the circumstances surrounding his death were suspicious and demanded a thorough investigation. The family has also alleged foul play, prompting police to question the wife as part of the probe.His father, Ramsevak Yadav, alleged that his son had been involved in a long-running dispute with his wife and suspected that he may have been murdered.Kiran also questioned whether Sanjeev, who she said weighed more than 100 kg, could have hanged himself, citing the video as suspicious.Police said Sanjeev, a native of Amritsar, married Manpreet, an Ambala resident, in April 2018 after the two met while working at Denso in Gurugram. The couple had a son in 2019, following which Manpreet left her job."We handed over the body to the family after the postmortem and are investigating the case from every angle. The postmortem report is awaited, which will reveal the exact cause of death. Further action will be taken as per the law," investigating officer Sub-Inspector Mahender Singh said.(With PTI inputs)
Article Summary: Sanjeev Yadav, 36, was found hanging at his home in Gurgaon's Surat Nagar. His wife, Manpreet Kaur, and their seven-year-old son were at home at the time. The child is believed to have recorded a video on a mobile phone showing his father hanging.

US President Donald Trump on Sunday claimed that the United States had been "locked and loaded" with military force against Iran at levels "not seen since World War II" but said he decided to call off the planned attack after Tehran and several Middle Eastern countries urged to hold off and pushed to make a deal.In a post on Truth Social, Trump said Iran had requested that Washington "hold off any attack" after the broad parameters of an agreement had been reached. "The USA is locked and loaded and ready to go against the Islamic Republic of Iran, at levels of Military Terror, Strength, and Power not seen since World War II," Trump wrote.Despite the military preparations, Trump said he had agreed to cancel the attack after being approached by Iran and other regional countries."Based on this request, I have agreed... to cancel the attack, subject to being able to rapidly make a DEAL," he added.According to Trump, the proposed agreement would include the "immediate, complete, and total" reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and "an end to Iran's nuclear threat."He also claimed that Israel had backed the decision. "The Country of Israel joins me in this commitment," Trump said, urging all parties to finalise the agreement."Get to work, everybody, and get it DONE," he added.Iranian authorities had not immediately commented on Trump's claims.This came after reports swirled that the US and Israel were planning a potential bombing campaign targeting Iran's energy infrastructure, with strikes possibly taking place over the weekend. According to CBS News, citing multiple US sources, officials discussed wrapping up the operation before financial markets open on Monday amid concerns over the potential impact of the strikes on the US and global economy.

NEW DELHI: Actor and BJP MP Kangana Ranaut has hit back at social media users sharing clips from her films and public appearances to criticise her recent remarks on protesters associated with the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP)-led agitation.In an Instagram story on Friday, Ranaut argued that clips showing her playing film characters or attending professionally organised events should not be used to suggest that similar behaviour was appropriate in everyday settings.Also read: 'Save your kids from evil feminazi, demonic leftists': Kangana on Noida girl's apology video “You want to use my movie character clips I get paid millions to play, high-profile show business events where I am surrounded by my own entourage and event planners, security forces, you want to use these to convince vulnerable teenagers that she can do the same on the road or in school functions or in dingy clubs? Is it the same thing,” she wrote.“Don’t mislead the youth; it’s not the same thing. Today you mislead other children; tomorrow it will be yours,” she added.Ranaut’s response comes amid criticism of her comments on videos emerging from the CJP-led protests at Jantar Mantar, news agency PTI reported.In an earlier Instagram post, the BJP MP from Himachal Pradesh’s Mandi had described videos from the agitation as a display of “filth, garbage and ugliness” and said the reels were “puke-inducing”.“So much ugliness in one place, these reels from GenZ protests are puke-inducing, the way they speak and the kind of language they are using, never in my life I have seen everything in each and every frame so jarring and so crass all at once, ewwww who is birthing and raising them?” she had said.Her remarks triggered criticism online, with users sharing clips from her films and other appearances in response.The exchange also comes after CJP chief spokesperson Saurav Das responded to Ranaut’s remarks about him, after she described him as a “28-year-old useless and unemployed” in an Instagram story.Das said Ranaut had received incorrect information about his age and professional background. He said he was 27, not 28, and clarified that he was a journalist rather than an active student.“I am a journalist, and I have never claimed to be an active student. I am a student of life. She should also strive to be one,” Das said.Das also addressed the use of derogatory language by some protesters during the agitation.He said individuals who believed they had been defamed could pursue civil or criminal defamation proceedings, but opposed the use of criminal justice machinery against protesters merely for objectionable language.He urged young people to exercise restraint in their choice of words while maintaining that objectionable remarks alone should not lead to criminal action.The online exchange comes amid continuing political and social-media debate over the conduct of protesters and the response to the CJP-led agitation.(With agency inputs)
Article Summary: Actor and BJP MP Kangana Ranaut has hit back at social media users sharing clips from her films and public appearances to criticise her recent remarks. In an Instagram story on Friday, she argued that clips showing her playing film characters or attending professionally organised events should not be used to suggest that similar behaviour was appropriate in everyday settings.

Article Title: Group waylays couple, thrashes engineer, gang-rapes fiancée in MP jungle
Article Text:
A couple was attacked and robbed near Hanuman Tekri shrine in Guna. (Image Used For Representational Purpose Only)





BHOPAL: A group of men waylaid an engineer and his 26-year-old fiancee and led them into a roadside forest in MP's Guna district late Thursday, where they allegedly gang-raped the woman and subjected her to brutal torture with a wooden stick besides thrashing and robbing the couple. Police formed an SIT to trace the perpetrators, who fled the scene.The horror unfolded near Hanuman Tekri shrine, about 25km from the district headquarters , when the couple was returning from the temple on a two-wheeler. Around 8pm, the group flagged them down near a petrol pump on the highway, claiming their bike had a flat tyre.The moment the engineer pulled over, the accused allegedly pounced on the couple, snatched the ignition keys, and forcibly dragged the duo into the nearby forest.The moment the engineer pulled over, the accused allegedly pounced on the couple, snatched the ignition keys, and forcibly dragged the duo into the nearby forest.The attackers then called in accomplices, the survivor told cops. The group rained blows on the couple, struck them with sticks, and snatched their cellphones and two-wheeler. The assailants later took the engineer away before sexually assaulting his fiancée, the complainant alleged.Hearing the couple’s desperate cries for help, a passerby alerted the Dial 112 emergency helpline.
Article Summary: A group of men waylaid an engineer and his 26-year-old fiancee and led them into a roadside forest in MP's Guna district late Thursday. They allegedly subjected the woman to brutal torture with a wooden stick besides thrashing and robbing the couple. Police formed an SIT to trace the perpetrators, who fled the scene.

Article Title: Uttarakhand CM Dhami hears public grievances, orders swift redressal
Article Text:
Uttarakhand CM Dhami hears public grievances, orders swift redressal





DEHRADUN: Uttarakhand chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami on Friday met people from different parts of the state at the Mukhya Sevak Sadan, located at the Chief Minister's Camp Office, and listened to their grievances. He directed concerned officials to ensure prompt and effective resolution of public issues.The chief minister also instructed officials from the chief minister's office, along with the Garhwal Commissioner and Inspector General (IG) of Garhwal, to accord top priority to the disposal of public complaints.He emphasised that there should be no unnecessary delay in resolving grievances and that timely relief must be provided to the affected citizens.On the occasion, Kedarnath MLA Asha Nautiyal met the chief minister along with a delegation and expressed gratitude to him for the successful and smooth conduct of this year's Kedarnath Yatra and the Char Dham Yatra so far.Nautiyal said that the state government's continuous monitoring and efficient management of the pilgrimage had helped ensure better facilities and a hassle-free experience for devotees.MLA Bhupal Ram Tamta also met the chief minister with a delegation and thanked the state government for prioritising local interests while addressing key issues related to the state's alpine meadows (Bugyals).The delegation said that Uttarakhand's Bugyals are an integral part of the state's natural and cultural heritage, with the livelihoods of many local residents and tourism activities closely linked to them. They stated that under the leadership of chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami, the state government has been consistently working to strike a balance between environmental conservation and the promotion of local employment, tourism, and livelihoods.The public representatives appreciated the government's efforts to promote development while taking into account the unique geographical and local conditions of the hill regions. They expressed confidence that better coordination between local interests, environmental conservation, and tourism development would create new employment opportunities in the mountainous areas and further strengthen the local economy.CM Dhami said that the state government's priority is the timely resolution of public grievances and the balanced development of every region of the state. He directed officials to address public issues with sensitivity, efficiency, and a sense of urgency.
Article Summary: Uttarakhand chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami on Friday met people from different parts of the state. He directed concerned officials to ensure prompt and effective resolution of public issues. Kedarnath MLA Asha Nautiyal met the chief minister along with a delegation and expressed gratitude to him for the successful and smooth conduct of this year's Yatra.

Article Title: Senthil Balaji gets pre-arrest bail from SC in Tasmac corruption case
Article Text: NEW DELHI: SC Friday granted pre-arrest bail to DMK's V Senthil Balaji in a corruption case related to Tasmac saying the state no longer suffers "from his so-called malefic influence". The court asked Balaji to scrupulously cooperate with the probe, not tamper with evidence or attempt to influence any witness and directed him to surrender his passport with the investigating officer. Seeking TN's response to Balaji's plea for quashing of the FIR, it warned him: "We will cancel or modify our order if there is breach of the bail conditions."
Article Summary: SC Friday granted pre-arrest bail to DMK's V Senthil Balaji in a corruption case related to Tasmac. The court asked Balaji to scrupulously cooperate with the probe, not tamper with evidence or attempt to influence any witness.

Article Title: Bhiwandi crash: Buiding owner, repairs contractor booked; state orders probe
Article Text:
A five-storey Bhiwandi building collapsed, killing ten people and injuring three others

Hundreds of dangerous buildings in MMR, thousands at risk (Photo credit: Santosh Gupta)





MUMBAI: The state govt ordered an inquiry into the crash of a part of a five-storey Bhiwandi building that claimed 10 lives.An FIR was lodged against the contractor hired for repairs, Ashok, and building owner, Bilal Khan, under Sections 105 (culpable homicide not amounting to murder) and 125 (negligent act endangering human life or personal safety of others) of BNS and relevant provisions of Maharashtra Regional and Town Planning Act for illegal construction, said DCP (zone 2), Thane, Pawan Basod.The PM announced an ex gratia of Rs 2 lakh each for the families of those killed and the CM Rs 5 lakh each.This was the third such major building collapse in Bhiwandi since 2020.Repairs began four days earlier after residents flagged falling plaster chunks and hired a contractor on their own. The building was not vacated during the work.Around 8pm on Thursday, residents noticed that a supporting pillar in wing B had developed a crack and was tilting, alerted the contractor and vacated the building.Workers were immediately brought in and the pillar was reinforced with iron support rods. Assuming that the structure had been stabilised, many residents went back into the building around 11.30pm.Moments later, half the wing collapsed, trapping many residents and labourers under the rubble.Over the next 15 hours, NDRF, fire brigade and Thane disaster response force personnel pulled out the bodies of Rakesh Paswan (25), Mukesh Paswan (30), Ashok Paswan (40), Krish Kumar (32), Ranjit Singh (45), Radheshyam Kushwaha (45), Siraj Rasul Sheikh (45), Shamim Ansari (32), Shyam Pal (40), and Santosh Pandey (42).Those injured, Abhay Yadav (26), Deepak Yadav (25) and Sangeeta Prajapati (36), were taken to a hospital. Some residents were rescued from the portion of the wing that remained standing.An NDRF officer said the building suffered a “pancake collapse”, in which one floor falls directly onto another.“The chances of survival in such collapses are extremely low. We deployed trained sniffer dogs to locate the victims.”Disaster management minister Girish Mahajan, who visited the site, said the repairs were carried out late at night to escape civic scrutiny.He directed the authorities to ensure that all dangerous buildings in Bhiwandi are vacated and appropriate action.Mehtab Ansari, a resident, told TOI that all flat owners had contributed around Rs 10,000 each for the repairs.Another resident, Komal Arvind Gupta, alleged that negligence during the work damaged the pillar.
Article Summary: An FIR was lodged against the contractor hired for repairs, Ashok, and building owner, Bilal Khan, under Sections 105 (culpable homicide not amounting to murder) and 125 (negligent act endangering human life or personal safety of others) The PM announced an ex gratia of Rs 2 lakh each for the families of those killed.

Article Title: Spain says most migrants return to Morocco after border rush kills 57
Article Text:
As thousands gathered near the border, Moroccan security forces used batons and tear gas to push back crowds

Spain said on Friday that it had regained control of a massive migrant surge into its North African enclave of Ceuta, with most of the more than 50,000 people who crossed the border by land and sea voluntarily returning to Morocco. The unprecedented influx left dozens dead and triggered political tensions across Europe.Spanish authorities said 57 bodies had been recovered on the Spanish side of the border. Officials warned that the death toll could be higher as there may have been additional casualties on the Moroccan side. According to the government, some migrants drowned while others were crushed as they attempted to climb the breakwater supporting the border fence.Spain's interior ministry said around 50,000 migrants entered Ceuta between Thursday and Friday, with about 48,300 having already returned to Morocco by Friday evening. Ceuta regional president Juan Jesus Vivas, however, estimated that the total number of crossings could have reached 60,000 over the two days.As thousands gathered near the border, Moroccan security forces used batons and tear gas to push back crowds and prevent more people from entering the Spanish territory.Reuters reporters at the scene also saw riot police firing tear gas, while water cannon vehicles were deployed to disperse migrants. Burnt remains of a bus and seven cars were visible following clashes.On the Spanish side, military vehicles were positioned along sections of the border as hundreds of migrants remained stranded on the Moroccan side. Several hundred people later crossed back through official checkpoints and openings in the fence, with many saying they were unable to find food or shelter in Ceuta. "I'm going back," one migrant told news agency Reuters.Spanish prime minister Pedro Sanchez travelled to Ceuta on Friday, where he faced protests and jeers from demonstrators. He described the mass border crossing as "a violation of Spain's territorial sovereignty" and said authorities were accelerating the return of those who had entered illegally with Morocco's full cooperation.The incident also exposed divisions within Europe over migration policy. Italy announced it was temporarily suspending the European Union's Schengen border-free travel arrangements with Spain, a decision that would affect air and sea travel between the two countries. Madrid criticised the move, saying it breached European Union treaties.Ceuta and Melilla, Spain's two autonomous enclaves in North Africa, form the European Union's only land borders with Africa. While both regularly witness attempts by migrants to enter Europe, Spanish authorities described the latest influx as unprecedented.Several right-wing political parties across Europe blamed the crisis on Spain's migration policies, including this year's amnesty for hundreds of thousands of undocumented migrants. Spain also summoned the Italian ambassador after Italian Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani claimed the amnesty had "encouraged human trafficking".US President Donald Trump also weighed in on the crisis, describing the situation at Ceuta as an invasion.The crossings "look like an invasion", Trump said, adding, "That same thing's going to happen to us if the Republicans don't get elected, except worse," referring to the upcoming US midterm elections.The US state department also criticised Spain's handling of migration, saying the incident was "the direct result of the Spanish Government's deliberate efforts to enable and facilitate mass illegal migration into Europe." It added, "We are considering actions to defend Americans at home and abroad from this threat and stand ready to assist other European allies considering similar option."Meanwhile, France said it would significantly strengthen security along its border with Spain.French interior minister Laurent Nunez announced that the police presence would be increased fivefold by Saturday, alongside enhanced aerial surveillance and additional patrols on trains.Spain's Guardia Civil police association AUGC also criticised the handling of the situation, saying there had been too few officers deployed at the border fence during the surge, leaving security forces unable to stop the mass crossings.
Article Summary: Spain says it has regained control of a massive migrant surge into its North African enclave of Ceuta. Most of the more than 50,000 people who crossed the border by land and sea voluntarily returned to Morocco. The unprecedented influx left dozens dead and triggered political tensions across Europe.
